title: Fallback reservoir and graceful containment controller
author: Elena Ramos
description:
Motivation: During a recent regional surge incident we observed repeated oscillation between regional eviction and full failover for mid-tier tenants. Root cause analysis showed aggressive immediate-eviction heuristics + global failover triggers interacting with best-effort KV-syncs and warm-up penalties. This PR introduces a lightweight fallback reservoir and a graceful containment controller that (1) absorbs short transient surges without triggering cross-region failovers, (2) staggers tenant eviction windows to reduce thundering rejoin, and (3) exposes a tunable containment tier that can be exercised by SLO enforcement policies.

What this changes: Implement a fallback reservoir (in-memory scoring + soft-lease) that temporarily holds eviction candidates for a configurable duration instead of evicting immediately. Add a containment controller that applies a progressive penalty schedule: initial soft-shed -> partial token cap -> full eviction only after reservoir expiry and penalty escalation. Introduce telemetry hooks and tracing spans for the reservoir lifecycle to aid incident analysis. Provide default conservative config that can be tightened by SRE on high-pressure events.

Design notes: The reservoir is per-region and tenant-aware; entries are lightweight structs (tenant_id, score, inserted_at, expiry_hint). Scoring uses a normalized SLO breach probability combined with recent CPU/RAM/queue-depth metrics. The containment controller runs as part of the regional load-shed orchestrator and defers actual node eviction calls for items in the reservoir until the penalty schedule advances. The controller also integrates with the existing circuit-breaker state machine; this PR adds a new reservoir state that circuit-breaker transitions can consult when deciding failover.

Backward compatibility: Runtime defaults to disabled if a feature-flag is not set. When enabled, the system falls back to the old eviction path if reservoir state cannot be loaded (safe fallback). No API changes to public endpoints.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for scoring, TTL eviction, and penalty escalation. Integration test simulating a burst workload to assert that immediate cross-region failover is avoided and that reservoir drains correctly under sustained pressure. Load tests against the canary fleet showed a 32% reduction in cross-region failover events for the simulated tenant mix and no measurable increase in tail-latency for surviving requests.

Deployment notes: Feature-flag gated rollout: start disabled, enable in a canary region for 24h, then roll global. Operators can tune reservoir_size, soft_shed_threshold, and initial_hold_ms via the console or configmap. Observability: new metrics (reservoir_size, reservoir_hits, reservoir_evictions, containment_penalty_level) and traces (reservoir.insert/reservoir.drain/containment.apply).

Related: ENG-2319 tracks the follow-ups to add automated canary tuning; SRE-502 covers runbook updates and alert threshold adjustments.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests for surge scenario
- [x] Metrics emitted with sensible names
- [x] Feature-flag and default disabled
- [x] Runbook draft attached to SRE-502

Notes: This is a pragmatic mitigation for repeated oscillation; follow-up PRs will refine scoring and introduce a bounded persistent reservoir for multi-process durability.

release_notes: Introduce a feature-flagged per-region fallback reservoir and containment controller to reduce unnecessary cross-region evictions during transient surges. Defaults disabled; operators can enable and tune via config. Metrics/traces added for observability.
notes_to_ops: Enable via feature flag 'containment_reservoir' in canary region; monitor reservoir_evictions and containment_penalty_level. If you see reservoir saturation, increase max_entries or lower soft_shed_threshold. See docs/runbooks/containment-reservoir.md for emergency rollback steps.
